audit_findings.evidence: support module source lines 109-190, 218-268, 358-398, 401-480; 12 independent offset-snapshot KL checks over 36 synthetic legal-span entries
audit_findings.finding: Mean-offset candidate features are flattened to one shared 512-vector and centered; the residual ridge direction matches H.T @ solve(H @ H.T + lambda I, r_centered/tau) on synthetic data. trust reuses this direction with up to five residual rounds, objective backtracking, and a per-offset reverse KL computed over all legal i<j spans.

ridge is one unconstrained analytic update; trust is at most five residual-ridge proposals under the full-span KL cap; unconstrained_ridge is five residual proposals without acceptance checks. Their result is not a matched iteration-count comparison.

P2 changes both the supervision geometry (stacked, separately centered offset features) and the objective (offset-specific detached targets with mean offset KL). A difference from mean-feature trust cannot be attributed solely to removing feature cancellation or solely to splitting the KL target.

audit_findings.area: P3 per-frame source cap and Adam proposal handling
audit_findings.evidence: source wrapper lines 15-54 and 145-255; core replay lines 31-53 and Adam helper lines 57-66
audit_findings.finding: The wrapper evaluates recomputed cached decoder boxes for every source frame after linearly interpolating the post-Adam parameter proposal. It accepts the first feasible alpha in the descending dyadic list. On complete rejection it restores both the pre-step parameter state and the pre-step Adam state, then clears gradients. On partial acceptance it retains Adam moments from the full proposal while using interpolated parameters; this is an Adam-proposal line search, not an Adam step recomputed at alpha-scaled learning rate.

The tested sequence stops at 2^-20 and contains no explicit alpha=0 trial. If every positive tested step violates the cap, the full-reject branch restores the source state; a feasible but smaller positive move is not searched.
